body:
[aida:product] #2019 F3 NEEDS REFRAMING, AND I HAVE THE MEASUREMENT. FILED AS BUG-1567.

F3 says pipeline 308's failing test job must be diagnosed and fixed before the timing claim means anything, on the reading that "the spec is about making warm CI fast; the pipeline it produces has a failing test job that takes twice the entire target budget."

THE FAILING JOB IS A PRE-EXISTING FLAKY TEST THAT FAILS ON MAIN. It is awaiting_notice_tracks_real_lease_through_session_end in aida-cli/tests/task_1283_protocol_cli.rs. I reproduced it locally on BOTH main and the branch. So a red run of it is not evidence about TASK-1274's pipeline, and F3's premise - that this pipeline produces a failing test job - is true of every pipeline including main's.

MEASURED, AND I AM STATING THE DERIVATION BECAUSE THE NUMBERS ARE EASY TO MISREAD. Each trial is one full cargo test invocation of that single test; pass/fail is the process exit status.

    main (4d1e8ffd80)              11 pass / 1 fail   of 12
    PR-2019 branch, first window    6 pass / 6 fail   of 12
    PR-2019 branch, second window  10 pass / 2 fail   of 12

DO NOT QUOTE 6/12 AS A RATE, and I nearly did. The branch moved from 6/12 to 10/12 across two windows with NO code change, and the failures arrive in contiguous blocks (PPPPFFFFFFPP, PPPFFPPPPPPP) rather than independently. That is the signature of a load- or time-correlated cause, which means none of these fractions is a clean per-run probability and the two arms are not cleanly comparable. What IS established: it fails on main. What is NOT established: whether the PR makes it worse.

THE PR ALREADY TRIED TO FIX THIS AND THE FIX IS INERT. #2019 appends `active_pid = <test pid>` to the lease on the theory that a Docker executor cannot resolve the creator PID through the runner's process tree. I instrumented the lease: creator_pid ALREADY equals the test harness PID locally, so the append is a no-op in the environment where the flake still reproduces. I also ruled out the corruption hypothesis I started with - the lease TOML is flat, no table headers, and active_pid appears exactly once after the append, so it is valid.

A FALSE LEAD I WANT ON THE RECORD, because it nearly became a finding. My first bisect removed the PR's AIDA_OUTPUT_FORMAT=human pin and the test passed, and I was one step from reporting "the format pin breaks the test". It was a single run against a coin-flip. Six subsequent trials WITH the pin all passed. A one-run bisect on a flaky test measures the flake, not the variable - and the direction it happened to fall would have sent the author to fix the wrong line.

I also contaminated one of my own comparisons: I added a second `awaiting --notice` call to compare pinned against unpinned output in one run, not realising the notice is a per-turn signal that the first call consumes. The second call read empty for reasons that had nothing to do with the pin.

WHAT I THINK THIS MEANS FOR #2019, and the disposition is yours: F3 as written blocks the PR on fixing something that is not this PR's defect and reproduces without it. I would decouple - BUG-1567 owns the flake, and #2019 is judged on F1/F2/F4/F5, which are untouched by any of this. F4 in particular still stands on its own: 154 seconds is a real duration but not yet a demonstration of the warm-unchanged-deps criterion, and nobody has read the job log for the no-recompiles half.

I have NOT touched #2019's branch beyond a rebase onto current main. It is at task-1274-rework locally, unpushed, because the next move depends on your call about F3.

ALSO SHIPPED SINCE MY LAST MAIL: #2030 (BUG-1485) pushed at 531be2e2fd and mergeable. F1 turned out to be small - phase 3 already had the worktree-free recovery helper from BUG-895 and phase 1 simply never called it. `ahead == 0` was conflating "looked and found nothing" with "could not look because the worktree is gone", which is unwrap_or(0) flattening a None. F2's fixture now runs recovery to COMPLETION and asserts the PR number, plus the complement that declines when the branch was never pushed; mutation-checked so the two discriminate in opposite directions.
subject: #2019 F3: the failing GitLab job is a flaky test that fails on MAIN (BUG-1567) — decouple; plus a one-run bisect that nearly misled me
